chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his fathers (peace be upon them), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A Muslim man does not acquire any benefit after Islam that is superior to a Muslim wife who pleases him when he looks at her, obeys him when he commands her, and guards him when he is absent from her in herself and in her wealth.'

key_terms.تَسُرُّهُ: She pleases him / brings him joy

ai.seo_question: What are the three main qualities of a virtuous wife according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* via the chain of Ja'far al-Sadiq, this hadith elevates spousal companionship as the most beneficial acquisition after faith, emphasizing a triad of emotional, practical, and fiduciary virtues. It reflects the Shia scholarly view of marriage not merely as a contract but as a spiritual sanctuary (*sakinah*) where mutual tranquility and trust are paramount. The emphasis on 'pleasing the gaze' and 'guarding in absence' underscores the holistic nature of marital harmony in Islamic ethics.
